StackType.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 25.) The 15 `on_stack` no-op overrides are DELETED; the base `Power.on_stack` adds, matching PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236), which adds unconditionally with no StackType branch -- PowerStackType.Single means 'Amount is hidden and displayed as 1' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13), not 'does not stack'. All 16 units re-verified against their own C#: 15 are StackType.Single, and NONE overrides InstanceType (PowerModel.cs:144 default None), so none needs T1's instance machinery instead of amount-adding. Two per-site exceptions, both verified: (1) DAMPEN's C# StackType is actually `None`, not Single (DampenPower.cs:22) -- the queue's 16-unit list was wrong about it; its only applier, MagiKnight, dedupes caller-side (MagiKnight.cs:78-96: re-application calls AddCaster only and never reaches PowerCmd.Apply), so the deletion is inert through the real caller and T28's caster-set machinery is untouched and re-pinned. (2) HEX genuinely reads Amount (HexPower.cs:79 feeds CardCmd.Afflict<Hexed>(card, Amount)), so this deletion closes a real divergence that remains DORMANT only because SpectralKnight's move machine never loops back to HEX and KnightsElite fields exactly one -- a second Hex applier makes it live. ILLUSION needed no override and is unchanged (the opposite-sign case the record notes). No reachable re-application among the other 13: Burrowed and Soar re-apply only after their own expire/remove, always onto a fresh instance. Pins: test/test_stack_type_single.py (39 tests).  The text it replaced read: The sim drops a re-application's offset citing PowerStackType.Single, which only means 'Amount is hidden' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13) -- PowerCmd.ModifyAmount:236 adds regardless. DORMANT: Smoggy reads Amount nowhere (it afflicts with the literal 1). One of the 15 units making this misreading (`py audit/tools/power_census.py stack`).

AfterCardEnteredCombat.issue: The structural gap is FIXED (all_cards now includes the Play pile, so a mid-play card is visible to the sweep exactly as C#'s AllCards has it). **BUT THIS ENTRY'S EVIDENCE NEVER HELD, and the record was wrong about the SIM, not merely stale:** on the tree it was written against, a non-Power card mid-play WAS already in all_cards (the old code parked it in the discard pile), so the described exposure was FALSE for every ordinary card. It was TRUE only for a POWER card mid-play, which HEAD put in no pile at all. The entry is also filed under AfterCardEnteredCombat while describing AfterCardPlayed. WHAT REASONING THIS REPLACES: the exposure claim itself, not just its currency.  The text it replaced read: Same pile-limbo shape as power/ringing's matching entry: the sim walks `getattr(self.owner, 'all_cards', ())`, and PlayerCombatState.all_cards (player.py:100-103) is hand + draw + discard + exhaust with NO Play pile, where C#'s PlayerCombatState.AllCards includes Play (PlayerCombatState.cs:70-80). Sharper here than for Ringing, because Smoggy's AfterCardPlayed sweep (powers.py:1748-1750) runs while the triggering Skill is itself mid-resolution: in C# that Skill is in the Play pile and IS afflicted with Smog, in the sim it is in neither all_cards nor the discard pile yet and is skipped -- so it can be replayed by an effect that returns it to hand, where the game would block it. PROMPT.md bug class 7. Reachable with any ported return-to-hand effect plus Living Fog. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.what: SmoggyPower.cs:41 the history query on AfterCardEnteredCombat
guards.rationale: C# asks the history whether a Skill was played this turn; the sim keeps the `_skill_played_this_turn` boolean (powers.py:1729, set at :1747, cleared at :1766 and :1776). Unlike power/ringing's ShouldPlay, the flag and the history agree here: this hook fires when a card ENTERS combat, never from inside the triggering Skill's own resolution, so the start-vs-finish difference cannot bite. Recorded as a divergence rather than faithful because it is the same substitution that IS observable on power/ringing, and a reader comparing the two should see that the difference is the call site, not the technique.

guards.what: SmoggyPower.cs:66-70 ShouldPlay tests only `Affliction is Smog`
